correctness.rationale: Smooth Birkhoff condition uniquely reduces the unit partner to ±(−r^{p−1}b,b), giving compact maximum of |F(p,r)|, endpoints zero. On the whole ratio interval F(2,r)=0 and its uniform first p derivative is g(r)=−√2 r log r/(1+r²), with a single strict maximum r0=e^(−u), u=coth(u). Interior analyticity gives the explicit half second derivative K(r), whose value at r0 is negative; uniform localization and implicit function theorem yield unique optimizer and linear drift. Independently differentiated the scalar formula to 50-digit precision at r0 and tested four nearby exponents, with residual/|ε|³ bounded about .115–.118. Finite optimization is not proof of uniqueness; uniform compactness plus IFT is.
